data.text: In iteration 1 the agent tested sulfide/ selenide substitutions and isovalent NASICON expansion for sodium solid electrolytes to keep stability against sodium metal and widen sodium migration pathways. Na3PSeS3 and Na3Zr2SiGePO12 were predicted stable with energy above the hull near 0.00 eV per atom and band gaps of about 2.3 eV and 4.2 eV respectively, and Na3PSeS3 showed sodium diffusion at 600 K tied with its parent. Na5PWS8 was predicted stable with energy above the hull about 0.02 eV per atom and a band gap of about 2.1 eV but failed contact with sodium metal because tungsten is reduced to metallic tungsten with a driving force of about 1.45 eV per atom. The agent concluded that S to Se anion mixing and isovalent Si to Ge NASICON expansion can retain passivation, while aliovalent tungsten for phosphorus introduces reducible d-metal reduction, and will next explore S to Se/Te mixing and isovalent NASICON expansion avoiding reducible cations.

reply.executive_summary: The search looked for new sodium solid electrolytes from Na3PS4 or Na3SbS4 that resist sodium metal and allow fast Na+ motion. The champion is Na3PSeS3 derived from Na3PS4, with space group Cc. Its energy above the hull is 0.002 eV/atom with an error bar of 0.002 eV/atom from the mean difference against density functional theory on 23 known compounds of Na-P-S-Se. Its computed band gaps are 2.266 eV and 2.931 eV. Its electrochemical window is 1.52 V to 1.7 V and it is passivating against sodium metal, so it is not thermodynamically stable at 0 V vs Na/Na+. Its diffusion coefficient at 600 K is 2.16e-07 cm²/s with an error of 1.42e-07 cm²/s, with a verdict of tied, meaning its range overlaps the parent and it cannot be called faster or slower. Literature shows this composition is already published in the Na3PS4-xSex family. The other finalists are Na3Zr2Ge2PO12 and Na6P2SeS7. One candidate was excluded for being non-passivating against sodium metal. Room-temperature ionic conductivity, density functional theory checks, cathode interface, grain boundaries, synthesis, element cost and experimental data were not computed. The candidates are computational predictions, not proven materials.
champion_reasons: The champion has the lowest energy above the hull per substitution at 0.018 eV, compared with 0.025 eV for Na3Zr2Ge2PO12 and 0.031 eV for Na6P2SeS7, so it comes first by the convention of lowest energy per substitution, not by a significant difference, with the three sharing the same ranking level.

It is the only finalist with a simulated diffusion coefficient at 600 K, at 2.16e-07 cm²/s with an error of 1.42e-07 cm²/s and a verdict of tied, while diffusion for Na3Zr2Ge2PO12 and Na6P2SeS7 was not simulated.

It derives from Na3PS4 with an electrochemical window of 1.52 V to 1.7 V, closer to 0 V than the 1.7 V to 3.28 V window of Na3Zr2Ge2PO12, and unlike Na3Zr2Ge2PO12 which derives from Na3Zr2Si2PO12 and is an oxide off the sulfide goal.
tradeoffs: Its window of 1.52 V to 1.7 V is narrow and not stable at 0 V vs Na/Na+, so stability against sodium metal relies on passivation with risk of thick interphase growth.
It is already published in the Na3PS4-xSex solid solution, so it is not a new composition, and selenide content brings moisture sensitivity and cost concerns.
It has no added sodium vacancies, leaving carrier concentration unoptimized, and its band gaps of 2.266 eV and 2.931 eV show electronic insulation but do not guarantee low interfacial resistance.
uncertainties: Energies are from a universal potential with an error bar of 0.002 eV/atom, not from density functional theory, which was not computed.
Diffusion was simulated at 600 K, not at 300 K, and calibration failed because ordered Na3SbS4 came out slower than Na3PS4, the reverse of experiment, so the verdict of tied is information only.
The diffusion error of 1.42e-07 cm²/s is large relative to the value of 2.16e-07 cm²/s, and room-temperature ionic conductivity was not computed with a range and method.

validation.text: Check phase purity and lattice by powder X-ray diffraction with Rietveld refinement against the predicted Cc cell.
Measure Na+ conductivity and activation energy by impedance spectroscopy as a function of temperature.
Test stability by cycling against sodium metal and analyzing the interphase by microscopy and spectroscopy.
Recompute the energy above the hull and the band structure with density functional theory.

synthesis.text: Ball milling followed by annealing under inert atmosphere could be tried for this sulfide-selenide family, without guarantee of success.

limitations: Room-temperature ionic conductivity was not computed, and no measured conductivity should be inferred.
Density functional theory checks, cathode interface, grain boundaries, synthesis, element cost and experimental data were not computed and are still needed.
Diffusion at 600 K cannot be presented as faster or slower conduction because calibration failed, and all candidates remain computational predictions, not proven materials.
